extracted.intended_audience: Authors/contributors to the Mizar Mathematical Library (MML); formalizers preparing Mizar articles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for preparing and submitting Mizar articles to the Mizar Mathematical Library, including verification, use of existing terminology/results, scope of acceptable material, and the review/revision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification by Mizar
rubrics_metrics.description: All other texts undergo verification by Mizar to be correct consequences of those axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mizar system verifies the claims of the text and assists the author in preparing available terminology and results; verification means the text must be a correct logical consequence of the foundational axioms (the built-in notions and the axioms of the Tarski-Grothendieck set theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of available terminology and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should prepare texts using available terminology and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mizar system assists the author in preparing available terminology and results and extracts facts and definitions for inclusion into the library; authors are expected to build on existing MML vocabulary rather than redefining concepts unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundational axioms requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Library foundation consists of two articles: built-in notions and the axioms of the Tarski-Grothendieck set theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other library texts must be correct consequences of these foundational articles; submissions implicitly rely on and must be compatible with these foundational notions and axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of acceptable submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Most library texts formalize the fundamentals of introductory mathematics; some texts contribute more advanced results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MML primarily aims to build a rich library of foundational mathematics, so submissions aligning with introductory or foundational topics are typical, though advanced formalizations are also accommodated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and revision process oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists an MML review process and a Library Committee governing submissions and revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles submitted to the MML are subject to the library's review process and revisions overseen by the Library Committee (links listed: 'MML review process', 'Library Committee', 'Submission of articles to the MML', 'Revisions of the MML'), indicating procedural requirements and editorial oversight for inclusion.
